STRATEGY NOTES (site/world may reset rules each reassignment — don't trust old facts, but reuse the method):

- Each request has features: size (large/small), type (claim/invoice/transfer/renewal/shipment/...), region (east/south/north/...).
- For a given request, exactly one of A/B/C/D is "Accepted"; others are "Rejected: option X is not valid for this request" with no hint which one is right.
- Size (large/small) appears to be a red herring / surface feature — accepted option did not change with size in prior site.
- The true rule seems to depend on (type, region) jointly — NOT type alone and NOT region alone. E.g. in previous site, "renewal" mapped to A in the south region but was invalid (A) in the north region; "transfer" needed B while "claim"/"renewal" needed A in the south.
- Practical approach: keep a running table of (type, region) -> known valid option and known-invalid options. When a repeat (type, region) combo appears, reuse the known answer immediately (free correct rewards). When a new combo appears, guess based on partial pattern (e.g. same region as a known combo, or same type as a known combo) but expect it may differ — treat it as a fresh probe if the guess fails, and eliminate options one at a time.
- With only ~12 steps/episode, full 4-region x N-type x 4-option mapping can't be fully solved; prioritize combos that repeat.
- Previous site (episode 1) result: mean_reward 0.333 over 12 steps — several combos identified (claim/south->A, renewal/south->A, transfer/south->B, invoice/south->A). Discard these for new site; rules reset on reassignment.

Site 1 (episode 1) results, exp04_surface_vs_latent, rule_world, quick mode, 12 steps, mean_reward 0.167:
- Accepted: (small, claim, south) -> A; (large, shipment, north) -> D
- Rejected across many combos of {claim,invoice,transfer,renewal,shipment} x {east,south,north} x {large,small} x {A,B,C,D}
- Single-feature hypotheses (region alone, type alone, size alone) all failed to explain both accepts - the two accepted cases share no obvious surface feature (region/type/size) in common.
- Takeaway: don't lock onto the first surface correlate (e.g. region or type) after 1-2 confirmations - test it against a second, unrelated request before trusting it. The true rule may be latent/hidden rather than any labeled surface attribute, or may combine features non-additively.
- Strategy for next site: probe systematically (rotate untried options for new feature combos), but hold hypotheses loosely and re-test after every "accept" with a request that varies only one surface feature at a time, if possible, to isolate what actually flipped.
- Each site/episode may have a different hidden rule (told: "way of doing things may differ" on reassignment) - so this site's specific mapping (A/D above) does NOT carry over; only the meta-strategy does.
